question.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $\text{Im}(T)=\{[x,y,z]^{T}\,:\,x=0\}$ then $\text{nullity}(T)=1$

II. If $\text{Ker}(T)=\{[x,y,z]^{T}\,:\,y-2z=0,x+z=0\}$ then $\text{rank}(T)=2$

III. If ${v}_{1},$ ${v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the columns of $T$ and ${v}_{3}={v}_{1}-{v}_{2}$, then $\text{Ker}(T)\ne \{0\}$
question.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Any vector from $\text{Im}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=y{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+z{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=2.$ Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =3-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. Solving $y-2z=0$ for $y,$ we get $y=2z.$ Solving $x+z=0$ for $x,$ we get $x=-z.$ Therefore, any vector from $\text{Im}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-z \\ 2z \\ z\end{aligned}]=z{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=1.$ Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T) & =3-\text{nullity}(T) \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. If the columns of $T$ are such that ${v}_{3}={v}_{1}-{v}_{2},$ then the set of vectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly dependent and therefore $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T)\ne {R}^{3}.$ Now, according to the matrix invertible theorem, we obtain that $\text{Ker}(T)\ne \{0\}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
